questions.question: What is Devise and how does it handle authentication in Rails?
questions.title: Devise Authentication Basics
questions.direct_answer: Devise is a gem that gives you a full authentication system — sign up, login, logout, password reset, confirmable, lockable — from a few generators. You add it to the Gemfile, rails g devise:install, then rails g devise User, which creates a migration (with encrypted_password, reset_password columns) and a User model with the Devise modules, and gives you helpers like current_user, authenticate_user!, and the sign in/out routes. It's built on Warden and gives you a tested, convention-over-configuration auth layer instead of writing login from scratch.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Rolling your own auth when Devise is the convention; or not understanding what Devise generates (migration + model + routes).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Devise gives you signup/login/logout/password-reset from generators (devise:install, g devise User). It builds on Warden and gives current_user and authenticate_user!.

sections.title: From Generator to Working Auth
sections.content:
devise:install sets up the config; g devise User generates the migration, model, routes, and helpers.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G[gem 'devise'] --> I[devise:install]
  I --> U[g devise User]
  U --> M[migration + model with Devise modules]
  U --> R[devise_for :users routes]
  U --> H[current_user, authenticate_user!]
```

sections.title: Setting up Devise
sections.content:
```ruby
# 1) Gemfile
gem 'devise'
# then: bundle install

# 2) Install
rails g devise:install

# 3) Generate the User model (migration + model + routes)
rails g devise User
# migration adds: encrypted_password, reset_password_token, reset_password_sent_at, ...

# 4) app/models/user.rb
class User < ApplicationRecord
  devise :database_authenticatable, :registerable,
         :recoverable, :rememberable, :validatable
end

# 5) Helpers now available in controllers/views:
current_user              # the signed-in user, or nil
user_signed_in?          # boolean
authenticate_user!        # before_action to require login

# 6) routes.rb (generated by devise_for :users)
new_user_session_path     # login
new_user_registration_path # sign up
destroy_user_session_path # logout
```
